# Preface {.unnumbered}

The following is an outline of the thesis, with checkmarks denoting whether the chapters are ready for review, including which papers of which I am a coauthor are mentioned or discussed in that chapter.

The hope is for this to be a "living document" of sorts, which I can keep updating after graduation.

This thesis is simultaneously compiled with [quarto](https://quarto.org/) 
into both HTML --- as a static website --- and PDF.
The HTML version is interactive, with hyperlinks, the possibility to see
internal and external references by mouse over, and a dynamic table of contents.
Also, several figures are rendered just-in-time from `python` code, 
which can be seen directly within the website.
This literate programming-like approach [@knuthLiterateProgramming1984] 
allows for reproducibility and transparency.
I did not, however, adopt it for all figures, as several of them are rather complex
and/or computationally intensive to generate.

## Anatomy of a gravitational wave

- the GW250114 detection, **area law paper** [@abacGW250114TestingHawkings2025] --- an outline of the qualitative results, deferring the technical details; all further discussions will use GW250114 as an example
- inspiral: how to get a simple PN waveform, chirp mass, mass ratio, chi_eff, tidal and so forth, HOM, precession, eccentricity **Revisiting GW150914 paper** [@gambaRevisitingGW150914Nonplanar2025]
- ringdown, the spectrum of a Kerr BH, mode excitation and why we didn't see the 33 and 44 modes for GW250114
- extrinsic parameters, the geometry of the detection tensor, the distance-inclination degeneracy
